How Fleet Edition
reaches its buyer
The buyer, the message per persona, the channels and what each costs, and the first ninety days from soft launch to scale.
read it as a field plan, not a forecast
Who signs, who uses, who blocks
Owns the fleet budget and the uptime number. Buys when a peer has already bought.
Lives in the tool nine hours a day. If the first week is hard, the deal dies at renewal.
Asks about data residency and SSO in the first call. Answer before they ask.
the blocker gets the first call, not the last
One promise per buyer, proof they can check, and a channel that carries it. Then ninety days, staged.
The promise, the proof, the channel
Partner referral, then an executive brief
Uses it nine hours a day
A two-week pilot on their own routes
Can block it in one call
The questionnaire, answered before they ask
if you keep one page, keep this one
Where the motion runs, and what each costs
Partners bring the cheapest pipeline; paid search the most expensive. The plan weights accordingly.
Of pipeline expected from partners and inbound
Paid search, capped at 10% of budget
Ten design partners live; every call recorded and reviewed on Friday.
Forty partners trained; the referral offer goes live.
Two reps on the top 300 accounts with the case study in hand.
Review by channel. Double the two that work; cut the one that does not.
we cut on the number, not on a feeling
Two points of uptime is a number my board understands. The pilot proved it in a fortnight, and dispatch never once called support.
the proof we carry into every first call
The failure modes we will watch
If dispatch leads need a call to get started, renewals fail in twelve months. Watch: setup completion without support.
Fleet buyers expect per-vehicle pricing. Per-seat confuses them. Watch: quote-to-close time.
Partners promise features that are not built. Watch: escalations mentioning a promise we did not make.
The full plan, the persona research and the channel model are in the go-to-market folder.
bring the objections, we want them early
